paragraphs: Here's what I want you to see, friend. Job, a man the LORD called blameless and upright (Job 2:3), pours out his pain in the rawest words you'll find, and the Bible just writes them down (Job 3:1-26). Nobody in this chapter tells him to be quiet. Nobody cleans it up. I think that tells us the Word has room for a hurting heart.

Notice what Job does NOT do. His wife told him, "Curse God and die!" (Job 2:9), and he curses the day he was born instead (Job 3:1). He asks why again and again, and he says it straight: "I am not at ease or quiet; I have no rest, for trouble has come." (Job 3:26). I'm not saying every word he says is the final word on the matter, because this story is a LONG way from over. I'm saying he brings his hurt out into the open instead of hiding it.

So when your own night gets heavy, you don't have to dress it up, baker. Honest sorrow is not the same as walking away from God, and a heavy heart is nothing to be ashamed of. And if a friend is in the dark, sit with them first and talk later, because sometimes the kindest thing is just staying put. Job's pain is real, and the rest of his story is still coming.
